Nontraumatic atlantoaxial rotatory subluxation; preceding infection or surgery does not make the syndrome itself an infectious disease.

Inherited disease of the vitreous and retina; neurologic ancestry does not establish extraocular nervous system damage across the group.
Intrahepatic portal venous sclerosis with portal hypertension; hypersplenism and leukopenia are frequent (30-79%), indicating splenic blood-organ dysfunction.
Vertigo specifically arising from central nervous system dysfunction; the generic definition's peripheral causes do not establish ear disease in this concept.
Immune-mediated pauci-immune glomerular injury despite absent ANCA; extrarenal manifestations are less common and not established at 30%.
Congenital vaginal obstruction is reproductive; associated uterine anomalies and amenorrhea do not establish endocrine or urinary disease.
Inherited vertical nystagmus is an ocular motor disorder; no additional brain or peripheral nerve disease is established by the supplied record.
Familial infantile nephrotic syndrome with defining ocular abnormalities; an immune mechanism is not established.
Neoplasm originating in the kidney during childhood; no additional organ involvement is shared across the umbrella.
Joint contractures, muscle hypoplasia and skin webs define disease; pulmonary hypoplasia is common (>30%) and often lethal. Cardiac hypoplasia frequency is uncertain.
